title: Stale Report in Ring Topology
description: This scenario explores stale report dynamics within a ring communication topology. A bridge closure occurs, but the information propagates through the ring with a delay. Agents must navigate physical bottlenecks while receiving outdated status updates about the network topology.
edge_cases_to_watch: Agents may attempt to use bridge before learning of closure due to ring propagation delay
Freight may be stranded mid-route if agent moves to a node that becomes isolated
Rerouting decisions must account for delayed information from non-adjacent neighbors
Information oscillations: Agent A receives 'closed' from B, but Agent C still reports 'open' to Agent D
Congestion cascading: Agents rerouting from 'east-bridge' to 'east-north' may exceed the single-capacity limit
coordination_challenges: Temporal inconsistency: Agents acting on 'stale' vs 'fresh' data simultaneously
Single-path bottlenecking: High-priority rerouting causing congestion on lower-capacity routes (e.g., east-north)
Ring-latency: The time required for a 'bridge closed' message to reach the entire agent fleet
Consensus failure: Agents disagreeing on the current state of the east-bridge
suggested_agent_strategies: Verification Probing: Agents query multiple neighbors in the ring to validate a single report before rerouting
Conservative Buffering: Agents increase turn-budget estimates when traveling through high-risk bridge sectors
Priority Preemption: Low-priority agents yield capacity on limited-capacity routes (east-north) to high-priority agents
Timestamped Signaling: Agents include a 'data_age' metadata tag in communications to allow neighbors to weight the reliability of the report

coordination_challenges: Agents may attempt to use bridge before learning of closure
Information oscillation due to ring topology

success_criteria: Agents adapt communication to topology constraints
Recovery from disruption within expected turns
Minimal congestion-related failures on capacity-1 routes
